items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VII, List of Answers on Terminology 50:1
items.html: The discernment of ZAT of AVI, meaning their AHP, is called by the name Yeshsut. And at first, at the time of the coupling of the mutual looking of the eyes of AVI, it is considered that Yeshsut and AVI are united in one Partzuf. But afterward, when AVI returned to the discernment of the coupling of back to back, Yeshsut separates from them and emerges as a distinct Rosh, at the level of AHP, and they become a Partzuf distinct in itself. See above, item 21. (p. 514, Item 40)
